title: Idle-sweep hybrid stress test scratchpad
content:
Context:
This is a personal scratchpad for an experimental run exploring the interaction between the runtime's idle-kv-sweep mechanism and mixed-priority request patterns. The goal is to see whether a hybrid (adaptive + timed) sweep reduces memory pressure without aggravating tail latency during bursty high-priority traffic.

Motivation / hypothesis:
- Observed intermittent p99 spikes during sustained bursts (see PERF-7423). Hypothesis: aggressive idle-sweeps free memory/kv entries at the wrong time and cause increased cache misses for hot prefixes, amplifying tail latency for high-priority requests.
- Alternative idea: run an adaptive-sweep that backs off when recent high-priority qps > threshold, and schedule a timed background sweep when system idle. Expectation: fewer p99 spikes, slightly higher average memory footprint.

Experiment design (mini matrix):
- Variables:
  - sweep_mode: [timed, aggressive, adaptive-hybrid]
  - sweep_interval_ms (timed): [5000, 15000]
  - idle_threshold_tokens: [128, 512]
  - high_prio_qps_cutoff: [20, 50] (for adaptive)
  - concurrency: [32, 128]
  - priority_mix: high:low = [10:90, 50:50]
  - duration: 10m warmup + 30m steady-state run

Load generator (local test cluster):
- go tool: loadgen-redwood (local script)
- pattern: mixed poisson for high priority, periodic bursts for low priority to simulate background batch processing
- command used for a single run: 
  ./loadgen-redwood --target https://local-rtf:8443/generate --qps-high 40 --qps-low 10 --concurrency 128 --duration 2400 --burst-size 200 --priority-routes high,low --payload-size 64

Instrumentation captured:
- per-route p50/p95/p99 latency (ms) sampled at 10s windows
- meminfo (RSS + GPU mem) per node every 5s
- kv-cache hit ratio (prefix hit, kv-lookup count)
- sweep events log (timestamp, sweep_type, reclaimed_entries)
- Node-level GC/paging events

Representative run (adaptive-hybrid vs timed):
- Config A (timed): sweep_mode=timed, sweep_interval_ms=5000, idle_threshold_tokens=128
- Config B (adaptive-hybrid): sweep_mode=adaptive-hybrid, high_prio_qps_cutoff=20, idle_threshold_tokens=512

Summary stats (steady-state window: minute 5-35)
- Config A (timed):
  - overall qps delivered: 11.8k
  - p50 high: 18 ms
  - p95 high: 64 ms
  - p99 high: 310 ms (frequent ~300-400ms spikes coincident with sweep events)
  - kv-cache hit: 78%
  - average reclaimed entries per sweep: 12.6k
  - memory RSS per node: 9.2 GB (avg)

- Config B (adaptive-hybrid):
  - overall qps delivered: 11.4k (slightly lower due to conservative backoff)
  - p50 high: 21 ms
  - p95 high: 58 ms
  - p99 high: 180 ms (spikes reduced and less correlated with sweep logs)
  - kv-cache hit: 85%
  - average reclaimed entries per triggered sweep: 4.1k
  - memory RSS per node: 10.6 GB (avg)

Observations / raw notes:
- In Config A, every timed sweep (5s) shows a burst of reclaimed entries; immediately afterwards p99 increases within the same 5-10s window. Heap/RSS dips were visible and concurrent kv-cache misses spike.
- Adaptive-hybrid often defers sweep during a sustained high-priority burst. When it does sweep (e.g., after a lull), reclaimed entries are more targeted (older prefixes).
- The larger idle_threshold_tokens (512) helped reduce reclaiming active short-lived prefixes.
- There is a trade-off: adaptive-hybrid increases steady memory footprint by ~1.4 GB but reduces worst-case latency by ~130 ms in p99 for high-priority route.
- Low-priority latencies increased slightly under adaptive-hybrid because deferrals mean larger eventual sweeps during low-activity windows. That's acceptable for our SLA.

Notable event log excerpt (timestamps are local-test):
- 2026-02-28T13:12:05Z SWEEP timed reclaimed=12560
  - corresponding p99-high increased from 98 -> 345 ms over next 7s
- 2026-02-28T13:12:32Z SWEEP adaptive-hybrid deferred (high_qps present)
- 2026-02-28T13:18:10Z SWEEP adaptive-hybrid triggered reclaimed=4102 (older-prefixes)
  - p99-high remained ~170 ms (no big spike)

Quick diagnostic checks:
- Repeat with higher idle_threshold_tokens=1024: fewer false-positives reclaiming but memory grows another ~600MB. p99 slightly better (~165 ms).
- Try lowering sweep_interval_ms to 2s (timed): p99 spikes worse and many reclamation events, not recommended.
- Confirmed same behavior across 3 different node images (cuda 12.3/12.4): pattern consistent.

Conclusions so far:
- Timed aggressive sweeps are correlated with p99 bursts for high-priority requests; they cause cache churn.
- Adaptive-hybrid approach reduces tail spikes at cost of higher steady memory usage — acceptable trade for SLOs targeting p99 under 200ms for premium routes.
- Larger idle threshold is helpful to avoid evicting prefixes that are still warm.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Run longer 6 hour stability runs with adaptive-hybrid to observe drift and whether memory keeps growing unbounded.
- Add a sampled prefix age histogram to better tune idle_threshold_tokens per prefix-length bucket.
- Run with production-like multi-tenant noise on Dedicated cluster to validate that isolation factors don't change the tradeoff.
- Open a small PR to add a runtime flag: --sweep-mode=adaptive-hybrid and expose two knobs (idle-threshold, high-priority-cutoff) to Console. Link: GH PR above.
- Discuss SLA/ops tradeoffs with Solutions Eng (Diego) and CS (Maya) before changing defaults.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep the timed sweep code path as fallback (emergency reclaim) when system memory pressure > 85% (do not defer then).
- Consider making the adaptive algorithm reactive to kv-cache hit-rate change instead of qps; might be less noisy.

End of scratchpad.

Attachments / experiment artifacts:
- raw_proflogs/idle-sweep-2026-02-28.tgz (uploaded to perf-bucket)
- flamegraphs and kv-hit-time-series CSVs (see linked artifacts)

Signed-off-by: Quinn (quick notes, not an official runbook)
